title: ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship
program_type: University merit scholarship considered automatically through the NUS undergraduate admission application (no separate scholarship application)
funding_type: Full subsidised tuition coverage plus annual living and accommodation allowances plus one-time computer allowance (university-funded; requires the MOE Tuition Grant)
administering_authority: National University of Singapore — Office of Admissions
implementing_agency: National University of Singapore — Office of Admissions (same body administers and processes the award; MOE administers the attached Tuition Grant and its bond)
programme_action: NUS Scholarships for Freshmen (International Students / Singapore Permanent Residents) — university-level scholarship tier
description: The ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship is a university-level NUS scholarship offered to support outstanding freshmen from ASEAN member countries excluding Singapore. Candidates are considered and shortlisted for the scholarship through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS, so there is no separate scholarship application. The scholarship covers 100% of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant and pays an annual living allowance, an annual accommodation allowance and a one-time computer allowance. Recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant, which carries a three-year post-graduation work bond for Singapore Permanent Residents and international students, and longer Ministry of Health service bonds apply in Medicine and Dentistry.

award_types: University-level full merit scholarship for freshmen
programme_structure.award_types_detail: NUS classifies the award as Scholarship Type: University-Level, Nationality: Singapore Permanent Residents / International Students, Student Type: Freshmen. It sits alongside the Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship, the NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship and The Association of Banks in Singapore – Goh Keng Swee Scholarship in the NUS Scholarships for Freshmen (International Students) list.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: The scholarship is renewed every semester provided the scholarship recipient maintains a Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and has good conduct. The scholarship is tenable for the normal candidature period.
programme_structure.intake: Annual intake, one per academic year, aligned to the NUS undergraduate admissions cycle. The most recent published admissions cycle is Academic Year 2027 / 2028.

status_note: The NUS Office of Admissions page for this scholarship publishes no scholarship-specific calendar deadline; consideration is automatic through the undergraduate admission application, and the published application period is 'Based on admissions application timeline'. The most recent cycle published on the NUS Important Dates page, Academic Year 2027 / 2028, shows the application windows (16 December 2026 to 4 January 2027 for NUS High School Diploma; 16 December 2026 to 3 February 2027 for Polytechnic Diploma from Singapore; 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027 for IB Diploma and for International Qualifications except IB; 18 February 2027 late afternoon to 19 March 2027 for Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level) all marked [Closed] with 'Application Form: CLOSED'. verification_notes: All award terms were read directly from the NUS Office of Admissions page for this scholarship, cross-checked against the NUS Scholarships Important Dates and Application page, the NUS Important Dates (admissions) page, the Office of the University Registrar undergraduate Fees page for the MOE Tuition Grant bond terms, the NUS AY2026/2027 Scholarship & Financial Aid brochure, the Undergraduate Admissions Publications page, the NUS Identity / Logo Guidelines pages, and three further NUS Office of Admissions pages (International Qualifications for Foreigners admission requirements, Other High School Qualifications, Application Overview). Ten official nus.edu.sg sources were fetched in total. Ten of the eleven NUS OM/AY URLs returned full content; the parenthetical-URL form of the scholarship page was required because nus.edu.sg serves some pages behind Incapsula bot protection, and the logo asset was separately retrieved with a browser user-agent and byte-verified as HTTP 200 image/png, 146x67 px. The NUS Identity site publishes the official NUS logo (modernised coat of arms plus NUS namestyle) and states the University name and logo are registered trademarks, so the logo is recorded as an official-domain asset of the awarding body.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: NUS undergraduate admissions application window for the applicant's qualification group. Published for Academic Year 2027 / 2028: 16 December 2026 to 4 January 2027 (NUS High School Diploma); 16 December 2026 to 3 February 2027 (Polytechnic Diploma from Singapore); 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027 (IB Diploma); 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027 (International Qualifications except IB Diploma); 18 February 2027 late afternoon to 19 March 2027 (Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level). All four windows are marked [Closed] on the page read on 2026-10-03.
application_deadline.application_period: Based on the NUS undergraduate admissions application timeline. NUS publishes no separate ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship application period, and all eligible students applying for undergraduate admission to NUS are considered for the scholarship.
application_deadline.official_rule: Quoted from the NUS Office of Admissions: 'All eligible students applying for undergraduate admission to NUS will be considered for this scholarship.' The NUS Scholarships Important Dates and Application page lists the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship application period as 'Based on admissions application timeline'. No scholarship-specific calendar date or timezone is published, so no deadline date is recorded here.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: There is no separate scholarship deadline, so a candidate cannot miss the scholarship by applying late for the scholarship alone; the binding date is the closing date of the applicant's NUS admissions qualification group, and the non-refundable application fee (S$20 for International Students with International Qualifications) must be paid by that closing date. NUS states that dates are subject to revisions, so the published window must be re-checked each cycle.

programme_duration.official_range: Tenable for the normal candidature period of the full-time undergraduate programme at NUS. NUS publishes no single year figure for the scholarship; it also covers students in Double Degree and Joint Degree Programmes and covers only the undergraduate programme for students in Concurrent Degree Programmes.
programme_duration.renewal_note: Renewed every semester provided the recipient maintains a GPA of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and has good conduct. The scholarship can be transferred across programmes, excluding Dentistry, Law, Medicine and Music; limited scholarships are available for Dentistry, Law and Medicine due to the competitive nature of these programmes. Overseas programmes must be completed before September of the year prior to graduation, and at least 75% of the credits or units required for graduation must be earned in Singapore, with no more than 25% obtained through overseas programmes.

funding.scholarship_type: University-level merit scholarship for freshmen, considered automatically through the admission application
funding.monthly_amount_note: NUS publishes the living and accommodation allowances as annual amounts (S$5,800 per annum and S$3,000 per annum). No monthly stipend is published and none is derived here.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel allowance is published for this scholarship in any official NUS source read.
funding.fully_funded_note: The award covers 100% of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant plus living, accommodation and computer allowances, but it is NOT unconditionally fully funded. Recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant, and Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who take up that grant are bonded to work for a Singapore-registered company for three years immediately after graduation; Medicine and Dentistry recipients additionally carry a six-year and five-year service bond respectively with the Singapore Ministry of Health. NUS estimates about S$6,000 for living expenses and S$5,750 for accommodation expenses per year as a full-time undergraduate, so the allowances do not cover every cost.

tuition.amount: 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees
tuition.conditions: Recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant. Covers students in Double Degree and Joint Degree Programmes, and covers only the undergraduate programme for students in Concurrent Degree Programmes. Does not cover the Concurrent Degree Programme in NUS Bachelor of Science and University of Melbourne Doctor of Veterinary Medicine. NUS publishes the remaining tuition fee payable after the grant at about S$8,300 to S$87,800 per annum depending on nationality and degree programme, but that range is not the scholarship amount.

bond.conditions: No bond is attached to the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship itself, but students are required to take up the MOE Tuition Grant to receive the scholarship. Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who take up the MOE Tuition Grant will be bonded under the terms of the Tuition Grant to work for a Singapore-registered company for three years immediately after graduation. Scholarship recipients admitted to Dentistry and Medicine will be required to undertake a service bond with the Singapore Ministry of Health for five and six years respectively. NUS does not guarantee employment upon graduation.

total_estimated_value.note: Not published, and deliberately not computed. NUS publishes annual allowance amounts only, so no four-year or total award value is stated or derived here.

coverage: 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant)
S$1,750 one-time computer allowance upon enrolment
Covers students in Double Degree and Joint Degree Programmes
Covers only the undergraduate programme for students in Concurrent Degree Programmes
coverage_limitations: Tuition coverage applies only to subsidised fees after the MOE Tuition Grant; recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant to receive the scholarship.

Taking up the MOE Tuition Grant creates a three-year post-graduation bond to work for a Singapore-registered company for Singapore Permanent Residents and international students, so the award is not unconditionally fully funded.
Scholarship recipients admitted to Dentistry and Medicine must undertake a service bond with the Singapore Ministry of Health for five and six years respectively.

The scholarship cannot be transferred to Dentistry, Law, Medicine and Music programmes; limited scholarships are available for Dentistry, Law and Medicine due to the competitive nature of those programmes.
The scholarship does not cover students in the Concurrent Degree Programme in NUS Bachelor of Science and University of Melbourne Doctor of Veterinary Medicine.

At least 75% of the credits or units required for graduation must be earned in Singapore, with no more than 25% obtained through overseas programmes; overseas programmes must be completed before September of the year prior to graduation.
NUS does not guarantee and/or provide scholarship recipients with employment upon graduation.
Recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance without prior approval from the University.

The allowances do not fully cover the costs of study. NUS estimates about S$6,000 for living expenses and S$5,750 for accommodation expenses per year as a full-time undergraduate, against a S$5,800 living allowance and a S$3,000 accommodation allowance.
Miscellaneous student fees charged to all students are not part of the scholarship coverage.
Exact benefit structure and amounts may differ in future cycles; the amounts above are those published on the official page read on 2026-10-03.
eligible_applicants: Citizens of an ASEAN member country, excluding Singapore
Applicants with strong leadership qualities and potential
Applicants with a good co-curricular activities record
Applicants possessing outstanding high school results
Applicants applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS
Freshmen applicants; transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible
final_year_condition: For a bachelor's-level award this applies to secondary/high-school completion: NUS requires applicants to have completed, or to be completing, high school with at least 12 years of general education by July in the year of application. For 'Other High School Qualifications', applicants who will be completing the high school final examination after the application closing date are expected to have a good pass certificate by end July, are not eligible for Dentistry, Law and Medicine under that route, and must submit standardised test results (Advanced Placement, ACT with Writing, SAT).
equivalent_degree_note: NUS admits applicants presenting a long list of international high-school qualifications for foreigners, including Indonesian Ijazah SMA, Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM), Thailand Certificate of Secondary Education (Mathayom 6), Vietnam National High School Graduation Examination, Unified Examination Certificate (UEC), international A-Level, American High School Diploma, IB Diploma, Indian Standard 12, Gaokao, HKDSE and others. Each qualification carries its own published admission requirements, and applicants must also meet the Programme Prerequisites for the programmes applied to.
previous_award_restriction: Scholarship recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance without prior approval from the University.

eligibility.citizenship: Citizens of an ASEAN member country, excluding Singapore. ASEAN member countries as listed by NUS: Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Outstanding high school results, and completion (or expected completion) of high school with at least 12 years of general education by July in the year of application. Programme prerequisites for the target NUS programmes must also be met.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Possess outstanding high school results. NUS does not publish a fixed percentage or grade cut-off for this scholarship, and admission is holistic.
eligibility.language_requirement: The scholarship page itself publishes no English-language test requirement. English requirements for admission are set per high-school qualification and per NUS programme; for example, the 'Other High School Qualifications' route lists the English Requirement as 'Not required', so no universal IELTS, TOEFL, PTE or Duolingo score is recorded here.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Have a good co-curricular activities record.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Have strong leadership qualities and potential.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance without prior approval from the University. No rule bars previous applications to the same award.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS as a freshman. Transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible. NUS has no direct credit transfer system that allows students to accelerate their studies; credit transfer, module waivers or course exemption requests may be submitted after enrolment and are subject to approval.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Open to full-time undergraduate degree programmes at NUS generally. The scholarship can be transferred across programmes, excluding Dentistry, Law, Medicine and Music. Limited scholarships are available for Dentistry, Law and Medicine. The scholarship does not cover the Concurrent Degree Programme in NUS Bachelor of Science and University of Melbourne Doctor of Veterinary Medicine.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: NUS publishes no fixed percentage, grade-point or rank threshold for this scholarship. The published criterion is 'Possess outstanding high school results', and shortlisted applicants are assessed 'based on the strength of their application'.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Applicants must meet the NUS Programme Prerequisites for the programmes they apply to, and present a high school qualification eligible for admission to NUS. Applicants presenting International Qualifications must have completed or be completing high school with at least 12 years of general education by July in the year of application. Qualification-specific requirements are published per qualification (for example Indonesian Ijazah SMA, STPM, Thailand Mathayom 6, Vietnam National High School Graduation Examination, UEC, international A-Level, American High School Diploma, IB Diploma).
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: NUS states that invited applicants will be assessed for scholarship suitability based on the strength of their application, and reserves the right to not award any scholarship if there are no candidates of sufficient merit. The decision of the selection committee is final and enquiries or disputes surrounding its decisions will not be entertained.

english_requirement.test_score_note: No English test score is published for this scholarship on any official NUS page read. English-language requirements are determined per high-school qualification and per NUS programme; the 'Other High School Qualifications' page lists the English Requirement as 'Not required' for that route, which is why no universal score is recorded here.

language_of_instruction.language_note: The ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship page and the NUS admissions pages read do not state a language-of-instruction rule for this award. NUS admission is based on the applicant's high school qualification and programme prerequisites rather than on a published medium-of-instruction restriction, so no language list is asserted here.

application_method.application_route: Submit an online application for undergraduate admission to NUS via the NUS Applicant Portal during the applicant's qualification-group application window. There is no separate scholarship application: all eligible students applying for undergraduate admission to NUS are considered and shortlisted for the scholarship through their admission application.
application_steps: Read up on NUS undergraduate programmes, shortlist choices and check that the Programme Prerequisites are fulfilled.
Confirm the correct applicant group and note the application period from the NUS Important Dates page.
Refer to the NUS Application Guide and Sample Form for the qualification being presented.
Submit one online application via the NUS Applicant Portal by the closing date of the applicant group.

Pay the non-refundable application fee electronically (Visa, Mastercard, AMEX, AliPay or PayNow) by the application closing date; the fee is S$20 for International Students with International Qualifications.

Submit all supporting documents via the Applicant Portal; the application is completed only upon receiving the acknowledgement email, submitting all supporting documents and paying the application fee.
Where applicable, update and submit final results within the required window (for example within 3 calendar days of release for AP, Gaokao, HKDSE, Indian Standard 12 and STPM).
Attend admissions assessment (interview and/or test) if shortlisted.
Track the application and admissions outcome via the Applicant Portal; admissions outcomes for International Qualifications are released progressively between March and July, latest by July.
Accept the admission offer online by the stipulated deadline in the electronic offer letter; the letter indicates whether the offer includes the MOE Tuition Grant.
If shortlisted, attend the scholarship selection interview (conducted January to July) and await the scholarship outcome, communicated by mid-July.
Complete the MOE Tuition Grant application and signing via the MOE Tuition Grant and Scholarships portal in September (Semester 1) or February (Semester 2).
application_method.application_fee: S$20 (inclusive of prevailing GST) for International Students with International Qualifications; S$10 for all applicants except International Students with International Qualifications. Non-refundable. Payment by Visa, Mastercard, AMEX, AliPay or PayNow only; overseas debit card, cash, bank transfer, internet banking and NETS are not accepted.

selection_process.decision_maker: NUS selection committee (Office of Admissions, National University of Singapore)
selection_process.selection_type: Competitive, invitation-only shortlisting from the admission applicant pool, with a selection interview stage
possible_stages: Consideration through the NUS undergraduate admission application (automatic; no separate scholarship application)
Shortlisting for scholarship suitability by an NUS selection committee
Email notification to shortlisted applicants only
Scholarship selection interview(s), conducted from January to July
selection_process.weighting_note: NUS publishes no weighting between the academic record, leadership and co-curricular record, and the interview. Shortlisted applicants are assessed 'based on the strength of their application'.
selection_process.results_timing: Selection interviews are conducted from January to July, and interviewed candidates will be informed of the scholarship outcomes by mid-July. Admissions outcomes for International Qualifications are released progressively from mid-May to end-July, latest by July.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: NUS reserves the right to not award any scholarship if there are no candidates of sufficient merit. The decision of the selection committee is final, and enquiries or disputes surrounding its decisions will not be entertained.

additional_factors: Citizenship of an ASEAN member country excluding Singapore
Full-time undergraduate admission to NUS as a freshman
Willingness to take up the MOE Tuition Grant, which is a condition of the award

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: A bachelor's degree (or a double, concurrent or joint degree as admitted) of the National University of Singapore at the end of the normal candidature period
possible_awards: Joint Degree (degree scroll jointly awarded by NUS and a partner university)
Bachelor's plus Master's under a Concurrent Degree Programme (the scholarship covers only the undergraduate programme)
degree_outcome.degree_note: The scholarship is tenable for the normal candidature period. It covers students in Double Degree and Joint Degree Programmes, and covers only the undergraduate programme for students in Concurrent Degree Programmes. Students who take longer than the normal candidature period under the modular system pay partial and then full non-subsidised fees, capped at 120% and 150% of the subsidised semestral fees for the first and second semester beyond normal candidature.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: NUS has no direct credit transfer system that allows students to accelerate their studies. Requests for credit transfer, module waivers or course exemptions may be submitted after enrolment to the relevant College, Faculty or School and are subject to approval. Separately, at least 75% of the credits or units required for graduation must be earned in Singapore, with no more than 25% obtained through overseas programmes.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: 100% of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees is covered, so recipients pay no subsidised tuition fee for the undergraduate programme covered. Recipients pay miscellaneous student fees, which are charged to all students whether registered full-time or part-time and are due at the same time as tuition fees. Recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant; those who do not complete the application and signing by the stipulated deadlines are charged non-subsidised tuition fees.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: The non-refundable application fee is payable by every applicant at the point of admission application (S$20 for International Students with International Qualifications), so it is not waived for scholarship candidates and is not refunded if the scholarship is not awarded.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: A Letter of Acceptance and Undertaking must be signed to accept the scholarship, and the MOE Tuition Grant undertaking must be completed and signed via the MOE Tuition Grant and Scholarships portal in September (Semester 1) or February (Semester 2).
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Miscellaneous student fees help meet part of the costs of healthcare for students, student cultural, social and recreational programmes, maintenance of the internal shuttle bus service, the IT network and other campus-wide services. Scholarship recipients are subject to the same fee payment procedures, late-payment penalties and refund policy as other students. NUS does not guarantee employment upon graduation.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: No bond is attached to the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship itself. However, students are required to take up the MOE Tuition Grant to receive the scholarship. Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who take up the MOE Tuition Grant are bonded under the terms of the Tuition Grant to work for a Singapore-registered company for three years immediately after graduation. Scholarship recipients admitted to Dentistry and Medicine are additionally required to undertake a service bond with the Singapore Ministry of Health for five and six years respectively. Students who do not wish to take up a Tuition Grant and its bond obligation pay non-subsidised fees throughout their studies.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: The official pages read state that students who do not wish to take up a Tuition Grant and its bond obligation will pay non-subsidised fees throughout their studies. Separately, if the scholarship recipient decides to withdraw from the University and/or terminate the scholarship prematurely, the University reserves the right to impose repayment of all scholarship monies disbursed to the scholar. No specific monetary penalty for breaching the MOE Tuition Grant bond itself is published on the NUS pages read.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm citizenship of an ASEAN member country other than Singapore
Confirm you are applying as a freshman, not as a transfer applicant
Check that your high school qualification is eligible for admission to NUS and that you meet the Programme Prerequisites for your target programmes
Check the application window for your qualification group on the NUS Important Dates page
Prepare your identification document, high school results and transcript, and an explanation of your grading system
Prepare standardised test results if your qualification route requires them
Prepare the application fee payment method (Visa, Mastercard, AMEX, AliPay or PayNow)
Submit the admission application and pay the fee before the closing date of your qualification group
Keep your email monitored (including junk/spam folders) for the shortlisting and interview invitation
Be available for a scholarship interview between January and July
Be prepared to accept the MOE Tuition Grant and its three-year work bond in Singapore after graduation

programme_comparison_fields.tuition_coverage: 100% of subsidised tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant
programme_comparison_fields.accommodation_allowance: S$3,000 per annum (compare NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship at S$5,000 per annum)
programme_comparison_fields.bond: Three-year MOE Tuition Grant work bond for a Singapore-registered company; six-year (Medicine) and five-year (Dentistry) Ministry of Health service bonds
programme_comparison_fields.separate_application: None; considered automatically through the NUS admissions application

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: There is no scholarship-specific essay or motivation letter for this award: candidates are considered and shortlisted on the strength of the existing NUS admissions application, and only shortlisted applicants are invited to a selection interview. Effort is therefore best spent on the admissions application itself (academic results, achievements, short response questions and co-curricular record) and on preparing for the interview, rather than on a separate scholarship statement.
profile_fit_labels: Willing to accept a Singapore work bond after graduation
common_mistakes: Assuming there is a separate ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship application with its own deadline; there is none, so the admissions application deadline is the only binding date
Applying as a transfer applicant, which makes the applicant ineligible for this scholarship
Expecting the scholarship to be awarded automatically on admission; only shortlisted applicants are contacted, and interviews run from January to July with outcomes by mid-July
Not budgeting for costs beyond the allowances: NUS estimates about S$6,000 for living expenses and S$5,750 for accommodation expenses per year, against allowances of S$5,800 and S$3,000
Overlooking the MOE Tuition Grant bond: a three-year obligation to work for a Singapore-registered company after graduation, six years for Medicine and five years for Dentistry
Planning an overseas exchange or summer programme that would push more than 25% of graduation credits outside Singapore, or that finishes after September of the year prior to graduation
Holding another scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance concurrently without prior University approval
Missing the document verification of original certificates at the start of term; NUS reserves the right to expel students who fail to turn up

risk_flags.risk: No separate scholarship application exists, so a candidate may believe the scholarship was applied for separately and may not realise consideration is entirely automatic through the NUS admissions application.
risk_flags.impact: A strong candidate could assume the scholarship was not applied for, or conversely delay preparing because there is no scholarship form to complete.
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the NUS undergraduate admissions application as the scholarship application and make it as strong as possible; NUS states all eligible students applying for undergraduate admission will be considered.

risk_flags.risk: The MOE Tuition Grant three-year work bond is a condition of the award and is easy to overlook when the award is described as covering 100% of tuition.
risk_flags.impact: A graduate who does not wish to work in Singapore faces a bond obligation, or would have paid non-subsidised fees instead.
risk_flags.mitigation: Record and communicate the bond explicitly. NUS states that those who do not wish to take up a Tuition Grant and its bond obligation will pay non-subsidised fees throughout their studies.

risk_flags.risk: Medicine and Dentistry carry Ministry of Health service bonds of six and five years respectively, and only limited scholarships are available for those programmes.
risk_flags.impact: A Medicine or Dentistry recipient faces a much longer service obligation, and the scholarship may be unavailable or competitive in those faculties.
risk_flags.mitigation: Check programme-specific availability and bond length before accepting; the scholarship cannot be transferred to Dentistry, Law, Medicine or Music.

risk_flags.risk: The scholarship is renewed every semester only if the recipient maintains a GPA of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and good conduct.
risk_flags.impact: Loss of the scholarship, including tuition coverage and allowances, if the GPA falls below 3.50 in any semester.
risk_flags.mitigation: Track cumulative and semester GPA against the 3.50 threshold and seek academic support early if grades slip.

risk_flags.risk: Only shortlisted applicants are informed by email, and interviews run from January to July with outcomes by mid-July.
risk_flags.impact: A candidate may receive no news for months and may assume an unsuccessful outcome; equally, an unmonitored email inbox could cause a missed interview invitation.
risk_flags.mitigation: Monitor the email address given in the application form, including junk and spam folders, throughout the January to July window.

risk_flags.risk: At least 75% of graduation credits must be earned in Singapore, and overseas programmes must be completed before September of the year prior to graduation.
risk_flags.impact: An exchange or overseas programme that is too long or too late can put graduation credits or the scholarship at risk.
risk_flags.mitigation: Plan overseas programmes within the 25% credit cap and before September of the year prior to graduation.

risk_flags.risk: The allowances do not fully cover living and accommodation costs, and miscellaneous student fees are charged separately.
risk_flags.impact: A residual annual funding gap of roughly S$3,000 for accommodation plus S$200 for living expenses based on NUS's own estimates, before miscellaneous student fees.
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget using the NUS Financial Aid Calculator and NUS living-cost estimates, and consider NUS financial aid, loans and bursaries for the residual.

risk_flags.risk: Application dates are explicitly subject to revision by NUS, and the cycle published at verification is closed.
risk_flags.impact: A candidate relying on a stale window could miss the cycle entirely.
risk_flags.mitigation: Re-check the NUS Important Dates page before each cycle; this record is scheduled for re-verification by 2026-12-01.

best_fit: High-achieving high-school leavers who are citizens of an ASEAN member country other than Singapore, want a research-intensive English-medium university in Singapore, have strong academic results alongside a demonstrated leadership and co-curricular record, and are willing to take up the MOE Tuition Grant and serve the resulting three-year work bond with a Singapore-registered company after graduation. Best suited to candidates who are comfortable with a competitive, invitation-only interview process and with renewing the award at a GPA of 3.50 or above each semester.

database_notes: Slot assignment: this file is slot 48, 'Singapore — National University of Singapore ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship'. A separate, already-complete record exists for Singapore Management University's ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship at research/bachelor/b132-smu-undergraduate-scholarships-international-students.json; the two are different awarding bodies and different awards, and neither overwrites the other.
Substitution: none. The assigned target exists on the official site under exactly the name 'ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship' and was recorded under that name.
NUS does not publish an acronym for this award. The short_title 'ASEAN UG Scholarship' is a derived short form, not an official acronym, and is flagged as such.

NUS lists the ASEAN member countries as Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam. Timor-Leste is included in the current list, so it is eligible in principle; Singapore is listed only as a member state and is expressly excluded from this scholarship.

The NUS Office of Admissions page for this scholarship states the scholarship applies to 'Singapore Permanent Residents / International Students' in its header while the eligibility criteria restrict it to citizens of ASEAN member countries excluding Singapore; the eligibility criterion is treated as controlling and Singapore citizens are recorded as ineligible.

The NUS Registrar page states the Ministry of Health service bond as 'five or six years for Singapore citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents/International students pursuing the medical programme respectively, and four or five years ... the dental programme respectively', which yields six years for Medicine and five years for Dentistry for international students and Singapore Permanent Residents. This matches the scholarship page's 'five and six years respectively' for Dentistry and Medicine. The six-year (Medicine) and five-year (Dentistry) figures are therefore recorded for the population this scholarship serves.

nus.edu.sg serves several pages behind Incapsula bot protection. The scholarship page returned full content only through the parenthetical URL form (https://www.nus.edu.sg/oam/scholarships/scholarships-for-freshmen-international-students/asean-undergraduate-scholarship), which is the same page as the canonical URL recorded in official_source_url; both URLs resolve to the same document.

The AY2026/2027 Scholarship & Financial Aid brochure confirms the award as 'Open to citizens of ASEAN countries (excluding Singapore)' and confirms that all eligible students applying for undergraduate admission to NUS are automatically considered with shortlisted applicants notified separately. The brochure also confirms that non-Singapore Citizens serve a three-year bond with a Singapore entity upon completion, and that all Medicine and Dentistry students must fulfil a four- to six-year bond with the Singapore Ministry of Health.

status is recorded as CLOSED because the most recent admissions cycle published on the official Important Dates page (Academic Year 2027 / 2028) shows all application windows as [Closed] with 'Application Form: CLOSED', and because the AY2026/2027 admissions exercise for International Qualifications closed on 23 February 2026. The next-cycle expectation is carried in status_note.

source_last_updated is null because neither the scholarship page nor the AY2027/2028 materials publish a visible last-updated date. The AY2026/2027 Scholarship & Financial Aid brochure PDF carries an internal LastModified date of 22 June 2026, which is not the same as the web page's update date and is not asserted here.

Because there is no separate scholarship application, application_method.direct_student_application is false and automatic_consideration is true. This is a deliberate distinction required by the schema: the award needs no scholarship form, but it is not automatic on admission either, since only shortlisted applicants are interviewed and only some are awarded.
No travel allowance, installation allowance, insurance, research allowance or book allowance is published for this award; each is recorded as unavailable rather than estimated.
All monetary amounts are in Singapore dollars (SGD) as published by NUS. No amount has been converted, totalled or annualised beyond what NUS publishes.
